summary: The strongest review frame is that the movie is powerful because of its "dedication to the politics behind its revolution." It is tense genre filmmaking, but it is also fiercely clear-eyed about strategy and power.
good_pick_if: you want a political thriller with real ideological bite
maybe_skip_if: you want the movie to soften or dilute its anger

summary: The best sincere review take is that it feels like a "big warm blanket" when you are down. The movie is melancholy and futuristic, but its real appeal is how gently it handles loneliness and longing.
good_pick_if: you want something tender, thoughtful, and a little wistful
maybe_skip_if: tech-romance as a premise just does not work for you

source_quotes.text: it takes a big warm blanket and wraps it around you

summary: The good review line here is that the flying is amazing, but the bigger surprise is that Cruise finally made a movie that "acknowledges his age." That gives all the blockbuster craft some real feeling underneath it.
good_pick_if: you want a huge crowd-pleaser that actually sticks the landing
maybe_skip_if: you want less military mythmaking in your action movies

source_quotes.text: Tom Cruise finally made a movie that acknowledges his age

summary: Calling it an "apology letter from marvel studios" is a funny way to say it has more feeling and personality than people expected. It is loud and goofy, but it actually lets the hurt matter.
good_pick_if: you want a blockbuster that remembers to have a heart
maybe_skip_if: you are fully burned out on Marvel no matter what

summary: One sharp read says it belongs in the category of AI stories about "how threatened men feel by the women around them." That lens fits: it is sleek, tense, and much more cutting than its polished surface first suggests.
good_pick_if: you want cerebral sci-fi with a real undercurrent of menace
maybe_skip_if: you want your AI stories less icy and more hopeful

summary: The observation that in the first alien movie "it’s the humans that invade the aliens" is part of why this still charms. It is playful, inventive, and so foundational that its handmade magic still feels fresh.
good_pick_if: you want a tiny piece of movie history that still feels alive
maybe_skip_if: silent-era theatricality does not connect for you

source_quotes.text: it's the humans that invade the aliens

summary: The review calling Brad Pitt asking the mafia if they want a hit "truly poetic cinema" gets the movie’s whole wavelength. It is violent, romantic, goofy, and powered by a very specific kind of delirious cool.
good_pick_if: you want something wild, quotable, and unapologetically heightened
maybe_skip_if: you want less violence and less nineties attitude

summary: The line "slow zombies are superior in every way" points at why this still rules. It is less about shock than watching a whole broken system shamble forward, with the mall setting turning consumer comfort into a trap.
good_pick_if: you want zombie horror with brains, atmosphere, and bite
maybe_skip_if: you prefer speedier, more modern horror rhythms

source_quotes.text: Slow zombies are superior in every way

summary: The "We belong dead" quote is one reason people never shut up about this movie. It is elegant, strange, funny, and surprisingly moving for something that still works perfectly as monster-movie iconography.
good_pick_if: you want an old horror movie with personality and pathos
maybe_skip_if: you want more full-bore terror than eerie charm

summary: That line about there being "nothing sacred" about the man in the ground tells you how scorched this movie is. It is grubby, fatalistic, and weirdly soulful beneath all the damage.
good_pick_if: you want a revenge-ish crime movie that feels spiritually wrecked
maybe_skip_if: you want redemption or polish instead of damage

source_quotes.text: There ain't nothing sacred about a hole in the ground
